ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows an OTL power amplifier circuit, with VT1 above and VT2 below, the two forming a complementary output stage; the emitters of VT1 and VT2 are connected at the middle output node, and this node is then connected to the load RL through the coupling capacitor C2, with the other end of the load grounded. The upper end of the power supply is labeled +VCC, the lower end is grounded, and the input signal enters the bias network through C1. Reasoning: The problem gives VCC = 20 V, the static potential of the VT1 emitter, that is, the output midpoint, is 12 V, the load RL = 4 Ω, and the transistor saturation voltage drop |UCES| = 0 V. The positive output swing is limited by the upper power supply, and the maximum upward swing peak value is 20 - 12 = 8 V; the negative output swing is limited by the ground potential, and the maximum downward swing peak value is 12 - 0 = 12 V. To ensure no distortion, take the smaller value as the maximum output voltage peak value, so Uom = 8 V. The sine output power Pom = Uom^2 / (2RL) = 8^2 / (2 × 4) = 64 / 8 = 8 W.

method.method_draft: First describe the circuit from the image: the joined emitters of VT1 and VT2 form the amplifier output, coupled through C2 to RL. From the text take VCC = 20 V, VT1 emitter/output quiescent potential VE_Q = 12 V, RL = 4 Ω, and |UCES| = 0 V. Compute the upward headroom as 20 - 12 = 8 V and the downward headroom as 12 - 0 = 12 V; the smaller value limits the undistorted peak output, so Uom = 8 V. Then calculate Pom = Uom^2/(2RL) = 8^2/(2×4) = 8 W.

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the natural single route for this circuit: identify the output node and determine the limiting voltage swing from the unequal DC headrooms, then convert peak sinusoidal load voltage to power.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the figure as an OTL complementary push-pull emitter follower: VT1 is connected toward +VCC, VT2 toward ground, their joined emitter/output node feeds the load RL through the coupling capacitor C2; the load voltage uo is across RL after C2.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the given numerical values: saturation voltage drop is zero, emitter potential of VT1 is 12 V, load resistance is 4 Ω, and supply voltage is 20 V.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use the OTL maximum undistorted sine-wave condition: the output-node peak amplitude is limited by the smaller DC headroom to either supply rail, reduced by transistor saturation voltage if nonzero. With |UCES|=0, Uom = min(VE_Q - 0, VCC - VE_Q). The load receives this AC peak through the coupling capacitor, so Pom = Uom^2/(2RL).
